requirements.quote:
QUIC packets that are determined to be lost are not retransmitted
   whole.  The same applies to the frames that are contained within lost
   packets.  Instead, the information that might be carried in frames is
   sent again in new frames as needed.
requirements.condition: When a QUIC packet is determined to be lost and its information needs to be sent again.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the lost information in new frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retransmit the lost packet whole or retransmit its contained frame instances.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-loss processing can be inspected to distinguish construction of new frames from whole-packet or frame-instance retransmission.

requirements.quote:
New frames and packets are used to carry information that is
   determined to have been lost.  In general, information is sent again
   when a packet containing that information is determined to be lost,
   and sending ceases when a packet containing that information is
   acknowledged.
requirements.condition: After a packet carrying retransmittable information is declared lost and until a packet carrying that information is acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the information again using new frames and packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue sending the information after a packet carrying it is acknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-and-acknowledgment trace can verify both the start and termination of retransmission.

requirements.quote:
*  Data sent in CRYPTO frames is retransmitted according to the rules
      in [QUIC-RECOVERY], until all data has been acknowledged.  Data in
      CRYPTO frames for Initial and Handshake packets is discarded when
      keys for the corresponding packet number space are discarded.
requirements.condition: While CRYPTO data remains unacknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit CRYPTO data according to the QUIC recovery rules until all of it is acknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime loss and acknowledgment traces can determine whether unacknowledged CRYPTO data remains scheduled for retransmission.

requirements.quote:
*  Data sent in CRYPTO frames is retransmitted according to the rules
      in [QUIC-RECOVERY], until all data has been acknowledged.  Data in
      CRYPTO frames for Initial and Handshake packets is discarded when
      keys for the corresponding packet number space are discarded.
requirements.condition: When keys for the Initial or Handshake packet number space are discarded.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard CRYPTO-frame data associated with packets in the corresponding packet number space.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation state can be checked at key discard to verify removal of the corresponding CRYPTO retransmission data.

requirements.quote:
*  Application data sent in STREAM frames is retransmitted in new
      STREAM frames unless the endpoint has sent a RESET_STREAM for that
      stream.  Once an endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame, no further
      STREAM frames are needed.
requirements.condition: When application data previously sent in STREAM frames needs retransmission and RESET_STREAM has not been sent for the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit the application data in new STREAM frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream loss trace can verify that retransmitted application data is placed in newly generated STREAM frames.

requirements.quote:
*  Application data sent in STREAM frames is retransmitted in new
      STREAM frames unless the endpoint has sent a RESET_STREAM for that
      stream.  Once an endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame, no further
      STREAM frames are needed.
requirements.condition: After the endpoint sends RESET_STREAM for a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Cease retransmission of that stream's application data in STREAM frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send further STREAM frames for retransmission on that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Post-RESET_STREAM output can be inspected for subsequent STREAM frames on the same stream.

requirements.quote:
*  ACK frames carry the most recent set of acknowledgments and the
      acknowledgment delay from the largest acknowledged packet, as
      described in Section 13.2.1.  Delaying the transmission of packets
      containing ACK frames or resending old ACK frames can cause the
      peer to generate an inflated RTT sample or unnecessarily disable
      ECN.
requirements.condition: When constructing an ACK frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the most recent set of acknowledgments.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not resend an obsolete ACK frame in place of constructing one from the most recent acknowledgment state.
requirements.why_checkable: The ACK ranges in an emitted frame can be compared with the endpoint's current acknowledgment state.

requirements.quote:
*  ACK frames carry the most recent set of acknowledgments and the
      acknowledgment delay from the largest acknowledged packet, as
      described in Section 13.2.1.  Delaying the transmission of packets
      containing ACK frames or resending old ACK frames can cause the
      peer to generate an inflated RTT sample or unnecessarily disable
      ECN.
requirements.condition: When constructing an ACK frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the acknowledgment delay from the largest acknowledged packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded acknowledgment delay can be checked against timing state for the largest acknowledged packet.

requirements.quote:
*  Cancellation of stream transmission, as carried in a RESET_STREAM
      frame, is sent until acknowledged or until all stream data is
      acknowledged by the peer (that is, either the "Reset Recvd" or
      "Data Recvd" state is reached on the sending part of the stream).
requirements.condition: After initiating stream cancellation with RESET_STREAM and before either the cancellation or all stream data is acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue sending the RESET_STREAM cancellation until the sending part reaches "Reset Recvd" or "Data Recvd".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not stop sending RESET_STREAM before either termination condition is reached.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream-state trace can verify repeated cancellation signaling and its exact stopping states.

requirements.quote:
The content of a RESET_STREAM frame MUST NOT change when it is
      sent again.
requirements.condition: When a RESET_STREAM frame is sent again.
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve the content of the previously sent RESET_STREAM frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not change any RESET_STREAM frame content across repeated sends.
requirements.why_checkable: Successive RESET_STREAM frames for the stream can be compared byte-for-byte or field-for-field.

requirements.quote:
*  Similarly, a request to cancel stream transmission, as encoded in
      a STOP_SENDING frame, is sent until the receiving part of the
      stream enters either a "Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd" state; see
      Section 3.5.
requirements.condition: After requesting cancellation with STOP_SENDING and while the receiving part has reached neither "Data Recvd" nor "Reset Recvd".
requirements.required_behavior: Continue sending the STOP_SENDING request.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue sending it after the receiving part enters "Data Recvd" or "Reset Recvd".
requirements.why_checkable: Emitted frames can be correlated with receiving-side stream state transitions.

requirements.quote:
*  Connection close signals, including packets that contain
      CONNECTION_CLOSE frames, are not sent again when packet loss is
      detected.  Resending these signals is described in Section 10.
requirements.condition: When loss of a packet carrying a connection-close signal is detected.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the connection-close signal again merely in response to detected packet loss.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss event for a CONNECTION_CLOSE packet can be followed to detect prohibited loss-triggered retransmission.

requirements.quote: *  The current connection maximum data is sent in MAX_DATA frames.
requirements.condition: When advertising the current connection maximum data.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the current connection maximum data in a MAX_DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type and encoded connection limit can be inspected in transmitted packets.

requirements.quote:
An updated value is sent in a MAX_DATA frame if the packet
      containing the most recently sent MAX_DATA frame is declared lost
      or when the endpoint decides to update the limit.  Care is
      necessary to avoid sending this frame too often, as the limit can
      increase frequently and cause an unnecessarily large number of
      MAX_DATA frames to be sent; see Section 4.2.
requirements.condition: When the packet containing the most recently sent MAX_DATA is declared lost or the endpoint updates the connection limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the updated connection maximum-data value in a MAX_DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Loss and limit-update events can be correlated with subsequent MAX_DATA output and its value.

requirements.quote:
*  The current maximum stream data offset is sent in MAX_STREAM_DATA
      frames.  Like MAX_DATA, an updated value is sent when the packet
      containing the most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream is
      lost or when the limit is updated, with care taken to prevent the
      frame from being sent too often.
requirements.condition: When advertising the current maximum data offset for a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the offset in a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted frame type and encoded per-stream offset can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
*  The current maximum stream data offset is sent in MAX_STREAM_DATA
      frames.  Like MAX_DATA, an updated value is sent when the packet
      containing the most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream is
      lost or when the limit is updated, with care taken to prevent the
      frame from being sent too often.
requirements.condition: When the packet containing a stream's most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA is lost or that stream's limit is updated.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an updated MAX_STREAM_DATA value for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Per-stream loss and limit-update events can be correlated with updated MAX_STREAM_DATA transmissions.

requirements.quote:
frame from being sent too often.  An endpoint SHOULD stop sending
      MAX_STREAM_DATA frames when the receiving part of the stream
      enters a "Size Known" or "Reset Recvd" state.
requirements.condition: When the receiving part of a stream enters "Size Known" or "Reset Recvd".
requirements.required_behavior: Stop sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames for that stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue sending MAX_STREAM_DATA frames for that stream absent a justified departure from the SHOULD requirement.
requirements.why_checkable: Post-transition packet output can be inspected for MAX_STREAM_DATA frames associated with the stream.

requirements.quote:
*  The limit on streams of a given type is sent in MAX_STREAMS
      frames.  Like MAX_DATA, an updated value is sent when a packet
      containing the most recent MAX_STREAMS for a stream type frame is
      declared lost or when the limit is updated, with care taken to
      prevent the frame from being sent too often.
requirements.condition: When advertising the stream limit for a given stream type.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the limit in a MAX_STREAMS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted frame type, stream type, and encoded limit can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
*  The limit on streams of a given type is sent in MAX_STREAMS
      frames.  Like MAX_DATA, an updated value is sent when a packet
      containing the most recent MAX_STREAMS for a stream type frame is
      declared lost or when the limit is updated, with care taken to
      prevent the frame from being sent too often.
requirements.condition: When a packet containing the most recent MAX_STREAMS for a stream type is declared lost or that type's limit is updated.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an updated MAX_STREAMS value for that stream type.
requirements.why_checkable: Per-type loss and limit-update events can be correlated with subsequent MAX_STREAMS transmissions.

requirements.quote:
*  Blocked signals are carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED,
      and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.  DATA_BLOCKED frames have connection
      scope, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames have stream scope, and
      STREAMS_BLOCKED frames are scoped to a specific stream type.  A
      new frame is sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for
      a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the
      corresponding limit.  These frames always include the limit that
      is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.
requirements.condition: When signaling connection-level blocking.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a connection-scoped DATA_BLOCKED frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type and its connection scope can be inspected in encoded output.

requirements.quote:
*  Blocked signals are carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED,
      and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.  DATA_BLOCKED frames have connection
      scope, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames have stream scope, and
      STREAMS_BLOCKED frames are scoped to a specific stream type.  A
      new frame is sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for
      a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the
      corresponding limit.  These frames always include the limit that
      is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.
requirements.condition: When signaling blocking for an individual stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a stream-scoped STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type and stream identifier can be inspected in encoded output.

requirements.quote:
*  Blocked signals are carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED,
      and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.  DATA_BLOCKED frames have connection
      scope, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames have stream scope, and
      STREAMS_BLOCKED frames are scoped to a specific stream type.  A
      new frame is sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for
      a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the
      corresponding limit.  These frames always include the limit that
      is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.
requirements.condition: When signaling blocking on the limit for a specific stream type.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame scoped to that stream type.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type and encoded stream type can be inspected in output.

requirements.quote:
*  Blocked signals are carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED,
      and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.  DATA_BLOCKED frames have connection
      scope, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames have stream scope, and
      STREAMS_BLOCKED frames are scoped to a specific stream type.  A
      new frame is sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for
      a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the
      corresponding limit.  These frames always include the limit that
      is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.
requirements.condition: When the packet containing the most recent blocked frame for a scope is lost and the endpoint remains blocked on the corresponding limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a new blocked frame for that scope.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a replacement blocked frame after the endpoint is no longer blocked on the corresponding limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Loss events and blocked state can be correlated with replacement blocked-frame transmissions.

requirements.quote:
*  Blocked signals are carried in DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED,
      and STREAMS_BLOCKED frames.  DATA_BLOCKED frames have connection
      scope, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames have stream scope, and
      STREAMS_BLOCKED frames are scoped to a specific stream type.  A
      new frame is sent if a packet containing the most recent frame for
      a scope is lost, but only while the endpoint is blocked on the
      corresponding limit.  These frames always include the limit that
      is causing blocking at the time that they are transmitted.
requirements.condition: Whenever a DATA_BLOCKED, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or STREAMS_BLOCKED frame is transmitted.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the limit that is causing blocking at transmission time.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a stale or unrelated blocking limit.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame's limit field can be compared with the active limiting value at the instant of transmission.

requirements.quote:
*  A liveness or path validation check using PATH_CHALLENGE frames is
      sent periodically until a matching PATH_RESPONSE frame is received
      or until there is no remaining need for liveness or path
      validation checking.  PATH_CHALLENGE frames include a different
      payload each time they are sent.
requirements.condition: While liveness or path validation is still needed and no matching PATH_RESPONSE has been received.
requirements.required_behavior: Send PATH_CHALLENGE frames periodically.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue periodic PATH_CHALLENGE transmission after a matching PATH_RESPONSE is received or the checking need ends.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed validation trace can verify repeated challenges and both stopping conditions.

requirements.quote:
*  A liveness or path validation check using PATH_CHALLENGE frames is
      sent periodically until a matching PATH_RESPONSE frame is received
      or until there is no remaining need for liveness or path
      validation checking.  PATH_CHALLENGE frames include a different
      payload each time they are sent.
requirements.condition: Each time a PATH_CHALLENGE frame is sent during a liveness or path-validation check.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a payload different from every payload used on earlier sends in that check.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse a prior PATH_CHALLENGE payload.
requirements.why_checkable: Payloads from successive PATH_CHALLENGE frames can be compared directly.

requirements.quote:
*  Responses to path validation using PATH_RESPONSE frames are sent
      just once.  The peer is expected to send more PATH_CHALLENGE
      frames as necessary to evoke additional PATH_RESPONSE frames.
requirements.condition: When responding to a particular PATH_CHALLENGE for path validation.
requirements.required_behavior: Send its PATH_RESPONSE once.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retransmit the same PATH_RESPONSE as loss repair.
requirements.why_checkable: Outgoing frames can be grouped by challenge payload to ensure exactly one response per received challenge.

requirements.quote:
*  New connection IDs are sent in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and
      retransmitted if the packet containing them is lost.
requirements.condition: When issuing a new connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Send it in a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted frame type and connection-ID field can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
*  New connection IDs are sent in NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and
      retransmitted if the packet containing them is lost.
requirements.condition: When a packet containing a NEW_CONNECTION_ID is lost.
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit the new connection ID in a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss event can be correlated with later transmission of the same connection ID.

requirements.quote:
Retransmissions of this frame carry the same sequence number
      value.  Likewise, retired connection IDs are sent in
      RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet
      containing them is lost.
requirements.condition: When retransmitting a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the same sequence-number value as the original frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign a different sequence number to the retransmission.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID sequence-number fields can be compared.

requirements.quote:
Retransmissions of this frame carry the same sequence number
      value.  Likewise, retired connection IDs are sent in
      RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet
      containing them is lost.
requirements.condition: When retiring a connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the retirement in a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted frame type and retired connection-ID sequence number can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Retransmissions of this frame carry the same sequence number
      value.  Likewise, retired connection IDs are sent in
      RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and retransmitted if the packet
      containing them is lost.
requirements.condition: When a packet containing a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame is lost.
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit the retired connection ID in a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet loss can be correlated with a later retirement-frame transmission for the same connection ID.

requirements.quote:
*  NEW_TOKEN frames are retransmitted if the packet containing them
      is lost.  No special support is made for detecting reordered and
      duplicated NEW_TOKEN frames other than a direct comparison of the
      frame contents.
requirements.condition: When a packet containing a NEW_TOKEN frame is lost.
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit the NEW_TOKEN frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A NEW_TOKEN packet-loss event can be correlated with a subsequent retransmission.

requirements.quote:
*  NEW_TOKEN frames are retransmitted if the packet containing them
      is lost.  No special support is made for detecting reordered and
      duplicated NEW_TOKEN frames other than a direct comparison of the
      frame contents.
requirements.condition: When detecting reordered or duplicated NEW_TOKEN frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Use direct comparison of frame contents.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not rely on special ordering or duplicate-detection support beyond direct content comparison.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's NEW_TOKEN duplicate and reorder handling can be inspected or instrumented to identify its comparison key.

requirements.quote:
*  PING and PADDING frames contain no information, so lost PING or
      PADDING frames do not require repair.
requirements.condition: When a PING or PADDING frame is lost.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not schedule loss repair solely for the lost PING or PADDING frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Loss handling can be tested to ensure these frames do not create retransmission obligations.

requirements.quote:
*  The HANDSHAKE_DONE frame MUST be retransmitted until it is
      acknowledged.
requirements.condition: After sending HANDSHAKE_DONE and until it is acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Retransmit HANDSHAKE_DONE as needed until acknowledgment.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not abandon HANDSHAKE_DONE retransmission while it remains unacknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: Loss and acknowledgment traces can verify that HANDSHAKE_DONE remains retransmittable until acknowledged.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints SHOULD prioritize retransmission of data over sending new
   data, unless priorities specified by the application indicate
   otherwise; see Section 2.3.
requirements.condition: When both retransmittable data and new data are available and application-specified priorities do not indicate otherwise.
requirements.required_behavior: Prioritize retransmission of data over sending new data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not prefer new data over retransmission absent contrary application priorities or a justified departure from the SHOULD requirement.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet scheduling decisions can be observed under simultaneous retransmission and new-data availability, with application priorities controlled.
